title: Petra and the Clock
premise: In 1917, Silas Blackwood — a woman living as a man to serve as a battlefield nurse — keeps a secret ledger of soldiers' true names, including Petra, an orphaned girl the unit has quietly adopted as their own. When a sealed letter arrives naming Silas's estranged family among civilians marked for evacuation from a collapsing front town, she discovers her brother orchestrated the plot that left Petra orphaned. With only one berth left on the last train and orders forbidding civilians, Silas must choose between the family that disowned her and the child who chose her; she gives the berth to Petra, smuggles herself out on foot with her brother wounded at her side, and ends the war with a new kind of family bound by chosen names rather than blood.
about_author: August Lockridge is the pen name of a former field archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime letters in provincial European collections. They write historical fiction about the people official records forget.

chapters.title: The Ledger of True Names
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Introduces the dressing station at Ypres salient's edge, her hidden identity, and the ledger where she records names soldiers are too afraid to speak. Emotional beat: quiet tenderness disguised as bureaucratic habit.

chapters.title: Petra of the Third Ward
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Eleven-year-old Petra, pulled from rubble two months prior, works as the ward's unofficial runner and mascot. The men teach her card games; Silas teaches her letters. Emotional beat: found family forming in miniature.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Seal
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A sealed military letter names civilians for priority evacuation from Verron — among them 'Blackwood.' Silas realizes it is her estranged family, and that someone high up knows her real name. Emotional beat: dread cracking open old wounds.

chapters.title: What the Orders Omit
chapters.summary: Major Halloway's POV. The major, who knows Silas's secret and protects it, explains the political plot: her brother Aldous sold information that doomed Verron's quarter, and the family name is being quietly erased. Emotional beat: complicity and reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Road to Verron
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Granted three days' leave under false pretenses, Silas travels to Verron, carrying Petra against orders after the girl stows away. Emotional beat: exasperation melting into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The House That Forgot Her
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Reunion with her mother, cold and formal; her father dead; Aldous absent. The house is full of portraits but no place set for her. Emotional beat: grief for a family that never claimed her.

chapters.title: Aldous Returns
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. The brother arrives by night, charming and desperate, revealing he brokered the artillery deal that destroyed Verron's east quarter — where Petra's parents died. Emotional beat: horror wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Petra Knows the Name
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra overhears Aldous's confession and recognizes 'Blackwood' from documents she salvaged from her ruined home. She says nothing, watching Silas. Emotional beat: a child learning adults lie to be kind.

chapters.title: The Bombardment Begins
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. German shells reach Verron ahead of schedule; the town's evacuation accelerates chaotically. Silas turns the family cellar into an aid post. Emotional beat: duty swallowing resentment whole.

chapters.title: Mother's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mother's POV. Silas's mother, learning of Aldous's guilt, chooses to protect him anyway and pressures Silas to use her military access to secure berths for the family. Emotional beat: the old wound reopened — duty to blood over truth.

chapters.title: The List of Berths
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the rail yard, Silas confronts the arithmetic: four family members, one legitimate berth, Petra entitled to nothing on paper. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizing into numbers.

chapters.title: Confession at the Yard
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra tells Silas what Aldous did, expecting to be disbelieved. Silas believes her instantly. Emotional beat: trust as the truest form of family.

chapters.title: Halloway's Price
chapters.summary: Major Halloway's POV. Halloway offers Silas a clean record and protection if she puts the Blackwoods on the train and lets Petra go to an orphanage convoy. Emotional beat: the institution demanding she amputate her own heart.

chapters.title: Night in the Cellar Aid Post
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Wounded civilians fill the cellar; Aldous, stricken by guilt, works beside Silas silently for the first time as an equal. Emotional beat: brotherhood rebuilt through labor, not words.

chapters.title: The Mother Decides Nothing
chapters.summary: Mother's POV. Pressed to choose which family member yields the berth, the mother freezes, revealing she never once chose Silas either. Emotional beat: the quiet verdict of a lifetime.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the platform, Silas puts Petra in the final berth, forging papers in their shared surname. Her mother boards; Aldous stays behind, wounded helping load stretchers. Emotional beat: love enacted as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Road Out on Foot
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas carries Aldous toward Allied lines through shelled countryside, the ledger heavy in her coat. They argue, laugh, and nearly die crossing a river. Emotional beat: reconciliation earned mile by mile.

chapters.title: What Halloway Knew
chapters.summary: Major Halloway's POV. Halloway intercepts them at a checkpoint, sees the forged papers, and burns them — choosing, finally, to spend his own career on mercy. Emotional beat: an institution bending to one act of grace.

chapters.title: Reunion at Calais
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra waits at the Calais hospital, having refused the orphanage convoy, and runs to Silas when she arrives with Aldous on a stretcher. Emotional beat: the family assembling itself by will.

chapters.title: Reading the Ledger Aloud
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Silas's POV. In the ward, Silas reads the ledger's names aloud so the wounded can hear themselves remembered; Aldous adds his victims' names in his own hand. Emotional beat: atonement as record-keeping.

chapters.title: The Armistice Bell
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. November 11th. Bells ring; the ward empties slowly. Silas, still legally a man, decides not to correct the record yet — some names are armor until the world is ready. Emotional beat: bittersweet survival.

chapters.title: Petra and the Clock
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, years later. Adult Petra, now a nurse herself, winds the station clock Silas left her and opens a fresh ledger of true names. Emotional beat: inheritance — love measured in what we carry forward.
